statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Current delayed NQ structure is two-way and does not verify persistent mean-reversion failure.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON; Tail remains below the block threshold outside the narrow open/PMI/post-release checkpoint.
headline: Low Tail, extreme Stress; the cash-open and PMI cluster remains the main conditional path-risk window.
body: Delayed December NQ is near 31,027 after trading roughly 30,998-31,095, leaving it materially below the session high rather than pinned to an extreme. VIX is near 14.2, the U.S. 10Y near 4.96%, and WTI near $90. Oil has eased, but Middle East diplomacy and rate sensitivity remain background catalysts.

lookbackSummary: Across the preceding 24 clock-hours, Tail was usually low, briefly reaching 27% around the prior U.S. open before falling back below WATCH; Stress remained high to extreme.
outlookSummary: Base-case Tail remains low outside the 13:30-15:30 UTC open/PMI/Fed/EIA cluster. Escalation requires observed persistent direction, shallow or failed retracements, repeated extension, or a coherent delayed second leg.

forecast.analysis: Delayed December NQ is near 31,027, about 68 points below the 31,094.75 session high and inside a roughly 97-point range. The retracement from the high does not verify persistent one-way or no-mean-reversion structure.
drivers: Delayed NQ is mid-range rather than holding the session high

forecast.analysis: Post-PMI price discovery overlaps Governor Barr at 14:05 and EIA at 14:30. Elevated Tail requires a coherent second directional leg or continued mean-reversion failure rather than headline importance alone.
After the main release cluster, Tail falls to WATCH if two-way trade returns. A delayed extension sequence or repeated failed retracements would keep the path risk above the low band.

forecast.analysis: Late U.S. morning risk remains WATCH if an earlier directional move still resists meaningful retracement. Normal counter-moves and fading cross-asset alignment would support further normalization.
drivers: Quality of counter-moves after the event cluster
Rates and oil as confirmation or conflict

forecast.analysis: Midday Tail remains at WATCH only if directional efficiency persists through lunch. A broader rotation with repeated retracements would keep the environment difficult but recoverable.
drivers: Breadth and semiconductor alignment if independently confirmed

forecast.analysis: Tail returns to the low band if the morning move has produced normal retracement depth and no fresh extension chain is developing. Stress remains extreme because the session may still digest the data cluster.
Into early afternoon, the base case is lower path risk if earlier extremes no longer hold. A renewed synchronized move in NQ, yields, volatility and semiconductors would be the main escalation route.
drivers: Renewed extension after a failed retracement

forecast.analysis: With the main U.S. data cluster behind the market, Tail stays low unless a fresh catalyst restarts directional efficiency. Stress eases as event-driven uncertainty decays.
Late-session risk is expected to remain low if the cash session has become rotational. A one-way power-hour continuation would be an exception that could lift Tail quickly.
Near the cash close, low Tail assumes no unresolved directional second leg. A closing auction that holds an extreme without retracement would invalidate that benign path.
After the U.S. close, Tail remains low if futures reopen without an abnormal gap or renewed catalyst. Stress continues to decline as same-day event risk clears.
Early Asia is expected to be lower risk absent a new geopolitical or policy shock. Any abrupt gap with sustained extension would be the primary conditional Tail trigger.
Asian-session Tail stays low under ordinary two-way trade. A fresh oil or policy shock would first raise Stress unless NQ also develops persistent directional structure.
drivers: Need for NQ path confirmation before Tail escalation

forecast.analysis: With no scheduled U.S. Tier-1 release in this hour, low Tail assumes normal retracement behavior. Cross-asset conflict would favor uncertainty rather than a mechanical Tail increase.
drivers: No scheduled U.S. release in this hour

forecast.analysis: Overnight risk remains low if price discovery stays balanced. Persistent movement toward an extreme with shrinking pullbacks would be the key invalidation signal.
The European morning begins with low Tail in the base case. A large gap or renewed rates-and-oil alignment would matter only if NQ also shows persistent extension.
As Europe becomes more active, Tail edges higher modestly because cross-asset repricing can transmit into U.S. futures. Two-way NQ trade would keep the increase limited.
Morning European liquidity can amplify moves, but Tail remains low unless NQ begins holding an extreme and rejecting meaningful retracements.
Approaching the later European morning, Stress rises gradually as the next U.S. data day comes closer. Tail stays low without actual evidence of one-way futures structure.
drivers: Current futures structure remains the Tail gate

forecast.analysis: The U.S. premarket approaches with low Tail but higher Stress. Any overnight trend must still demonstrate shallow pullbacks and repeated extension before Tail can leave the low band.
Premarket participation should increase, lifting Stress. Tail stays just below WATCH unless an extreme holds persistently or a new catalyst creates repeated directional extension.
By 10:00 UTC Thursday, claims and other U.S. releases are drawing closer but remain ahead. Stress rises on event proximity; Tail stays low until path evidence shows mean-reversion failure.
drivers: Event importance raises Stress before Tail
Mean-reversion failure remains the Tail trigger
